where: Section 2: The page fault and its cost
problem: When a victim frame is reused, the handler never invalidates the victim page's PTE. The old PTE still has valid 1 and points to the frame, which now holds a different page, so a later reference to the victim page can read the wrong page.
fix: After writing a dirty victim back (if dirty), set the victim's PTE valid bit to 0 and record its swap/backing location before reading the new page into that frame.

where: Section 2: The page fault and its cost
problem: The handler says the needed page is read from swap space and a dirty victim is written to swap space. File-backed pages, such as mmap pages or program text, come from and go to their file, not swap.
fix: Say the page is read from its backing store: swap space for anonymous pages or the mapped file for file-backed pages. Likewise write a dirty victim to its backing store.

problem: The expression 1 ÷ 2.500062502 × 10⁻⁶ is evaluated left to right as (1 ÷ 2.500062502) × 10⁻⁶, not as 1 ÷ (2.500062502 × 10⁻⁶), so the written expression does not equal 399,990.

It says all shared pages are marked read-only and that a write by either process causes a COW copy. A page that was already read-only, such as a code page, must not be copied on a write; writing it is a protection error.
fix: Say shared writable private pages are marked copy-on-write/read-only. A write to an originally read-only page remains a protection fault, not a COW copy.
